title: Tribu
deck: Issue electronic payment documents to SUNAT from TypeScript in one call: no XML to write, no IGV to compute, no SUNAT codes to type.

blocks.text: In Peru every formal sale must be issued as an electronic document to SUNAT. Without a library that means computing IGV, writing UBL 2.1 XML, signing it with the digital certificate, zipping it, sending it over SOAP and decoding the response receipt (CDR).
Every step has rules SUNAT only reports after sending, with unclear error codes.

Tribu turns the whole process into one call. It computes the amounts, validates the document against SUNAT's rules *before* sending, builds and signs the XML, sends it and returns one plain JSON `Record` for you to save.

blocks.caption: Issuing an invoice: IGV, XML and signing are handled by Tribu.

blocks.source:
flowchart LR
  A[sunat.invoice] --> B[Compute amounts and IGV]
  B --> C{SUNAT rules}
  C -- error --> X[Error with suggested fix]
  C -- ok --> D[UBL 2.1 XML]
  D --> E[XMLDSig signature]
  E --> F[ZIP + SOAP]
  F --> G[(SUNAT)]
  G --> H[CDR]
  H --> R[JSON Record]
blocks.caption: Fig. 1 — The issuing pipeline: rules are checked before touching the network.

items: **Server only.** Tribu holds the certificate and SOL password, so `tribu.create` refuses to run in a browser.
**Your database numbers.** `nextNumber` is a callback: sequencing is guaranteed by your transaction, not an in-memory counter.
**Actionable errors.** Every validation error says which field fails and how to fix it, before wasting a submission.
**Pluggable transport.** A custom `transport` can target an OSE without changing anything else.

head: Area
Covered in v0.1
rows: Invoices, receipts (individually or in a daily summary), credit and debit notes
General and the reduced rate for restaurants and hotels

items.label: document types accepted by SUNAT beta

blocks.text: SUNAT's beta environment accepts every document type Tribu issues. It ships as experimental until verified in production, and the README explains how to report that experience without exposing credentials.

quote: You never write XML, never compute IGV and never type a SUNAT code by hand.
